records.name_note: Only NC State has a dedicated page for this exact taxon among the sources checked. It is titled Hoya bella and lists Hoya lanceolata subsp. bella and Hoya paxtonii as former names, so trade literature using the subspecies name should be matched to this record. NC State's Common Name(s) list is alphabetized and Miniature Wax Plant is its third entry; the first entry is Beautiful Hoya, and the page's description prose also leads with "the beautiful hoya", so Beautiful Hoya is recorded as common_name and Miniature Wax Plant is an alternate name on the same page.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's page for Hoya bella carries the tags "#non-toxic for dogs" and "#non-toxic for cats" in its Tags field. The full tag run is: #houseplant #partial shade #climbing plant #trailing #container plant #cascading #hanging baskets #white flowers #vine #non-toxic for dogs #non-toxic for cats #twining #greenhouse plant #slow growing #conservatory plant. The Plant Type field lists Epiphyte, Houseplant, Perennial, Vine. The scope is cats and dogs as tagged on this species' own page. The page has no Poison block, no poison-part list, no symptom list, no severity rating and no handling warning, so human toxicity and edibility are not addressed. Nothing was borrowed from other Hoya species.
records.water_dry_down_target: allow the soil to become almost dry before watering
unknowns: Only NC State Plant Toolbox (plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/hoya-bella/) was confirmed as a dedicated page for this exact name. RHS URLs for hoya-bella and hoya-lanceolata-subsp-bella returned 404. MoBot, UF/IFAS and Clemson pages could not be read in this session: the sandbox proxy refused www.missouribotanicalgarden.org and edis.ifas.ufl.edu, and plantfinder.mobot.org and ask.ifas.ufl.edu were also refused. Nothing was borrowed from those sources or from other Hoya species, so cross-source corroboration and disagreement are unchecked.

common_name: researched as 'Miniature Wax Plant'; landed as 'Beautiful Hoya'. NC State's alphabetized Common Name(s) list is Beautiful Hoya, Beautiful Wax Plant, Miniature Wax Plant, Pretty Waxflower, Waxflower; Beautiful Hoya is its first entry and the description prose's lead name ('The beautiful hoya is ...'). Miniature Wax Plant is the third entry on the same page and is kept as an alternate in name_note.

toxic_to_pets=false rests only on NC State's '#non-toxic for dogs' and '#non-toxic for cats' tags for Hoya bella. There is no Poison block, symptom list or severity rating, and no second source was checked.

day_f_min and day_f_max (75 to 85) come from a single NC State sentence about warm temperatures the plant thrives in. The page does not split day from night, so night_f_min and night_f_max are null. chill_damage_f is null because the page only says cold drafts can cause leaf damage, with no onset temperature. Zones 11 to 12 are a hardiness rating, not a damage-onset temperature.
humidity_need=average is a mapping of NC State's stated 50 to 60% humidity. The source does not use the words average, low or high.

water_regime=dry_thoroughly_between is a judgment from 'allow the soil to become almost dry before watering'. 'Almost dry' could also be read as dry_surface_between. The page notes the semi-succulent leaves store some water, and that overwatering and poor drainage can cause root rot. No day interval, check depth or dormant-season guidance is stated, so those fields are null.

soil_base=standard_potting follows the page's wording, 'a loamy, well-drained potting mix'. The page lists Soil Texture as Loam (Silt) and Sand, and Plant Type includes Epiphyte, but it does not describe a chunky or bark mix, so chunky_aroid and orchid_bark were not used. soil_drainage is null because the page gives only a bare Good Drainage with no moisture pair, which is ambiguous. soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are null because the page lists Acid (<6.0), Neutral (6.0-8.0) and Alkaline (>8.0), and the open-ended bands set no bounds.

light_fc_min, light_fc_good and direct_sun_hours_max are null. The page says 'bright indirect sunlight' and that early-morning or late-afternoon direct sun may encourage flowering, with no foot-candle or species-specific hour figure. The 2-6 hours in the structured Light field is the site-wide category legend and was not used. outdoor_sun_exposure=part_shade comes from the structured Light field 'Partial Shade' and applies only in USDA zones 11 to 12. The page also says direct sunlight can cause leaf scorch.

Size: the Dimensions block gives Height 1 ft to 2 ft and Width 1 ft to 2 ft, converted to 12-24 in. The description frames this as a cascading, trailing vine 'in length', so height is vine length rather than an upright height.

Fertilizer fields (fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months, fertilize_strength) are not addressed on the page and are null. is_edible and attracts_pollinators are null because the page has no Attracts field and says nothing on edibility. The Play Value field lists Attractive Flowers, Easy to Grow and Fragrance, but that is not a pollinator statement.

records.name_note: Sources agree on the genus: RHS has separate pages, with Goeppertia rufibarba marked Name Status Correct and Calathea rufibarba marked Synonym, and NC State's page for Goeppertia rufibarba lists Calathea rufibarba under 'Previously known as:'. RHS's Goeppertia rufibarba page adds 'Previously included within the genus Calathea'. Both NC State and RHS give Furry Feather Calathea as the lead common name and list Velvet Calathea as an additional name (RHS under Other common names; NC State as the second entry of its alphabetized Common Name(s) list), so Velvet Calathea is not used as the lead.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's page for this exact species carries the tags "#non-toxic for cats" and "#non-toxic for dogs" in its Tags line, which reads in full: "#ornamentals #houseplant #perennial #non-toxic for cats #herbaceous perennial #container plant #fuzzy #green leaves #interiorscape #non-toxic for dogs #evergreen #hairy stems #hairy leaves #partial shade tolerant". These tags are scoped to cats and dogs only. The page has no Poison block, no symptom list and no human-toxicity rating, so nothing is stated about people or other animals.
unknowns: No admissible source states chill_damage_f; NC State's USDA zones 11a-12b are a hardiness rating, not a damage-onset temperature, so it is null.
day_f_min/day_f_max/night_f_min/night_f_max are null: NC State gives one room-temperature range (65 to 75 degrees Fahrenheit) with no day/night split, so it was not split into day and night fields.

light_fc_min and light_fc_good are null: NC State says only 'bright, indirect light' with no foot-candle figure. direct_sun_hours_max is null because the '2-6 hours' text is NC State's generic Partial Shade legend, not species prose; NC State's species prose says 'direct sun light can cause the leaves to scorch'.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are null: NC State lists Acid (<6.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0), and the Acid band is open-ended; RHS lists pH as 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral', so no ceiling can be set.

fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_active_months and fertilize_strength are null: NC State says only 'Fertilize the plant monthly during the spring and summer', a word-based cadence with seasons rather than a stated day count, month list or dilution. RHS's fertiliser advice sits in a Cultivation paragraph that reads as genus-level and was not used.

water_dry_down_target, water_check_depth_cm and the day-estimate fields are null: no admissible species source gives a dry-down depth or interval. water_regime keep_moist rests on NC State's 'moist but not wet or soggy' sentence; NC State also warns that overwatering can cause root rot.

RHS gives size as Max Height 0.5-1 metres (19.7-39.4 in) and Max Spread 0.1-0.5 metres (3.9-19.7 in), which differs somewhat from NC State's Height 2-3 ft and Width 1-2 ft; the NC State Dimensions block was used as the anchor.
RHS lists Partial shade and NC State lists Partial Shade, so outdoor_sun_exposure is part_shade only; NC State hardiness zones 11-12 mean this is a houseplant in most of North America.

Edibility is not addressed by any admissible source and pollinator attraction is not mentioned, so is_edible and attracts_pollinators are null. MoBot, Clemson, UF/IFAS, Penn State, UMD and UGA were not found to have a dedicated page for this species, and the MoBot Plant Finder was not reachable in this run.

The non-toxic tags are NC State's only toxicity statement for this species; no second admissible source was found to confirm or contradict them. NC State also lists a separate genus page for Goeppertia, which was not used.

records.name_note: NC State's dedicated page for Euphorbia tithymaloides lists Pedilanthus tithymaloides and Tithymalus tithymaloides under 'Previously known as', so older care sheets under Pedilanthus refer to this same plant, filed here under Euphorbia; the page adds that the epithet means resembling the genus Tithymalus, 'which is now a synonym for Euphorbia.' NC State's Common Name(s) list is alphabetized (Devil's Backbone, Japanese Poinsettia, Myrtle-leaved Spurge, Redbird Flower, Slipper Flower, Zig Zag Plant), its first entry is Devil's Backbone, and its description opens with 'The devil's backbone is an erect succulent shrub'. Only NC State was reachable among the admissible sources, so no other source disagrees on the name.
records.toxicity_detail: Source: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox page for Euphorbia tithymaloides. The page's intro line says "This plant has low severity poison characteristics." Its Poison block sits under the human-scoped "Poisonous to Humans" heading: Poison Severity: Low. Poison Symptoms: "The milky white latex sap found in all plant parts can cause mild to severe contact dermatitis. If contact with the eyes occurs the sap can cause temporary to permanent damage to the cornea. If eaten, blistering can occur on lips and oral mucosa. Avoid ingesting plant parts and keep plants away from pets and children." Poison Toxic Principle: Diterpene esters. Causes Contact Dermatitis: Yes. Poison Part: Sap/Juice. Handling warning (the same Symptoms text): the milky latex sap in all plant parts can cause mild to severe contact dermatitis, and sap in the eyes can cause temporary to permanent damage to the cornea. The Problems field, separate from the human-scoped Poison block, lists Contact Dermatitis, Poisonous to Humans, Problem for Cats, Problem for Children, Problem for Dogs. Plant Type field: Houseplant, Poisonous, Shrub. Page tags: #red flowers #poisonous #milky sap #houseplant #shrub #problem for children #problem for dogs #problem for cats #contact dermatitis #container plant #poisonous if ingested #clumping. toxic_to_pets=true rests only on the Problem for Cats and Problem for Dogs values; the page gives no cat- or dog-specific symptoms or severity, and its "keep plants away from pets" sentence names no animal.
records.water_dry_down_target: Water this plant when the soil becomes dry 1 to 2 inches below the surface.
unknowns: Only NC State (plants.ces.ncsu.edu) could be read for this exact taxon. MoBot (plantfinder.mobot.org / missouribotanicalgarden.org) was unreachable from the sandbox (ConnectError, TLS failure), Clemson HGIC returned HTTP 403, and no dedicated RHS or UF/IFAS page for Euphorbia tithymaloides or Pedilanthus tithymaloides could be located. UF/IFAS and CAES pages in the cache that mention it are multi-species tables, so they were not used.
soil_ph_max left null: NC State's Soil pH is 'Neutral (6.0-8.0)' and there is no RHS pH field to check a ceiling against. soil_ph_min 6.0 is the floor of that closed band.

Temperatures: NC State's prose gives one 60 to 85 degrees Fahrenheit range with no day/night split, so day_f and night_f are null. No chill-damage onset temperature is stated (zones 9a-11b is a hardiness rating, not a damage onset), so chill_damage_f is null.
humidity_need left null: NC State says 'Average to high humidity is well-tolerated', which describes tolerance, not a need, and gives no percentages.

light_fc and direct_sun_hours_max left null: the page says the plant 'prefers bright, indirect light' and 'The foliage can burn from too much direct sunlight', with no foot-candle or hour figure. outdoor_sun_exposure keeps only part_shade. NC State's structured Light field also lists Full sun, but the same page warns "The foliage can burn from too much direct sunlight." and says the plant "prefers bright, indirect light", so full_sun was dropped.

water_regime: NC State's structured Soil Drainage field (Good Drainage, Moist) was not used for watering. The watering sentence (water when soil is dry 1 to 2 inches below the surface) falls between dry_surface_between and dry_thoroughly_between, and dry_surface_between was chosen. The same page warns 'Overwatering can cause root rot.' and 'Leaf drop will occur if the soil is too dry.' water_check_depth_cm 2.5 is the 1 inch low end of the stated 1 to 2 inch (2.5 to 5.1 cm) range. No day-interval figures are stated, so water_growing_days_est and water_dormant_days_est are null.

soil_base cactus_succulent rests on NC State's prose 'well-drained, potting mix that is used for succulents'. The structured Soil Drainage (Good Drainage + Moist) gives soil_drainage moderate, not fast.
No fertilizer information on the NC State page, so the fertilize fields are null.

Toxicity: NC State's Poison block is human-scoped (Poisonous to Humans, severity Low). toxic_to_pets true rests only on the Problem for Cats and Problem for Dogs values (Problems field and tags), with no cat- or dog-specific symptoms. The page's 'keep plants away from pets and children' sentence names no animal and is not used as pet evidence. is_edible false rests on the Poison Symptoms sentence 'If eaten, blistering can occur on lips and oral mucosa. Avoid ingesting plant parts ...'; no source says any part is eaten as food.

Mature size is NC State's whole-species Dimensions block (Height 2 ft to 10 ft, Width 1 ft to 2 ft), converted at 12 in per ft. The page's cultivar notes give different sizes (e.g. 'Nana' up to 12 inches, 'Variegata' up to 8 feet); these are cultivar-specific and were not used.
Pollinators: NC State's Attracts field lists Hummingbirds only.
Not kept distinct in the record but noted: this is a separate taxon from the landed Euphorbia milii, E. pulcherrima and E. tirucalli; no data from those species or from the genus page was used.

records.name_note: Plerandra elegantissima is the name on both admissible pages reached (NC State and RHS). RHS lists Aralia elegantissima, Dizygotheca elegantissima and Schefflera elegantissima as synonyms, and NC State lists Dizygotheca elegantissima and Schefflera elegantissima as previously known as. Both pages give the common name false aralia.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's tag line for this page reads: "#houseplant #evergreen #interiorscape #fantz #non-toxic for cats #non-toxic for horses #non-toxic for dogs #container plant". Its Plant Type field lists Shrub and Tree. This page carries no Poison block, so there is no NC State human-scoped severity rating. These are NC State's Problem-for-Cats/Dogs-style tags, here the non-toxic variants, and are separate from any Poison block. RHS separately carries a handling flag in its Potentially harmful field: "Contact may cause skin allergies. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling". RHS names no animal in that flag, and it does not contradict NC State's cat and dog tags. No oxalate listing is carried over from the schefflera genus. Neither page addresses eating the plant.
unknowns: The Missouri Botanical Garden pages for this taxon (taxonid=359828 and kempercode=b619) could not be fetched in this session (connection errors, including through the plantfinder.mobot.org redirect), so nothing is taken from MoBot. No Clemson HGIC or other admissible page for this exact name was found.
UF/IFAS publication FP180 covers this plant only under the synonym name Dizygotheca elegantissima, not the dedicated Plerandra elegantissima name, so it was not cited for any field.

NC State's page has no Poison block and no Dimensions block. toxic_to_pets=false rests on NC State's non-toxic for cats and non-toxic for dogs tags alone. RHS's Potentially harmful skin-contact flag names no animal.

water_regime keep_moist rests on NC State's description sentence about keeping the potting soil moist. It is not a structured watering field. RHS's structured Moisture field reads 'Moist but well-drained', which is a softer counterpoint. No watering interval or dry-down depth is stated, so those fields are null.
soil_base is set from NC State's phrase 'potting soil' only. RHS's compost advice is under glass and may be genus-level text, so it was not used.

outdoor_sun_exposure lists only part_shade, the value both pages support. NC State also lists Full sun for Light (a generic legend hour range sits inside that tag, so direct_sun_hours_max is null). RHS lists Full shade, which NC State does not. Both are left out and disclosed here.
soil_ph is null: RHS lists acid, alkaline or neutral, and NC State gives no pH.

No source gives air temperature ranges, chill-damage onset, humidity percentages, light in foot-candles, fertilizer guidance, edibility or pollinator attraction. NC State's USDA zones 10a-12b and RHS's H1B rating are hardiness ratings, not damage onset.

NC State's description says the plant can reach tree size, but it gives no dimensions. Size comes from RHS's Max Height 2.5-4 metres (98.4-157.5 in) and Max Spread 1.5-2.5 metres (59.1-98.4 in), converted by x39.37. These are for the whole species, not cultivar sizes.

records.toxicity_detail: NC State's page for Peperomia serpens carries the tags "#non-toxic for cats", "#non-toxic for horses" and "#non-toxic for dogs", so the non-toxic claim is scoped to cats, dogs and horses only. These are tags; the page has no Poison block, no symptom list, no poison-part list, no handling warning and no severity rating. The full tag list is: #easy to grow #houseplant #herbaceous perennial #epiphytic #drought tolerant #tropical #humidity tolerant #hanging baskets #well-drained soil #evergreen #non-toxic for cats #non-toxic for horses #non-toxic for dogs #perennial #low maintenance #pet friendly. Its Plant Type field lists four values: Epiphyte, Herbaceous Perennial, Houseplant, Vine. Edibility is not addressed. No other admissible source with a page for this exact name could be loaded to confirm or contradict the tags.
unknowns: Only NC State (plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/peperomia-serpens/) has a dedicated page for this exact name among the admissible sources I could load. RHS has no page at /plants/peperomia-serpens or /plants/peperomia-scandens (HTTP 404), and its genus page and site search never mention serpens. Clemson returned HTTP 403, and the UF/IFAS and Missouri Botanical Garden fetches failed with proxy errors. I found no species page there, so every field rests on NC State alone.

toxic_to_pets is false based only on NC State's tags '#non-toxic for cats' and '#non-toxic for dogs' (the page also tags horses). The page has no Poison block or symptom data, and no second admissible source confirms it.

chill_damage_f, the day and night temperature fields and the cool-rest note are null. NC State only says 'Avoid cold drafts and maintain a moderate temperature', with no figures. Its USDA zones 10a-12b are a hardiness rating, not a damage-onset temperature.

humidity_need is average, taken from 'maintain a moderate temperature and humidity'. The page also tags the plant '#humidity tolerant' and lists Humidity under Resistance To Challenges. No humidity percentages are given.

light_fc_min, light_fc_good and direct_sun_hours_max are null. The description says 'bright, indirect sunlight', but gives no footcandle figure. The '2-6 hours' text sits inside NC State's site-wide Partial Shade legend, so it is not species-specific and was not used.
outdoor_sun_exposure is part_shade only, from NC State's Light field: 'Dappled Sunlight' (mapped to part_shade) and 'Partial Shade'. Zones 10-12 make this mainly a houseplant.
soil_drainage is moderate, from NC State's 'Good Drainage' plus 'Moist' pair and the sentence 'moist, well-drained soil'. soil_base is null because no potting-mix type is named.

water_regime and the other watering fields are null. NC State gives only 'does not tolerate overwatering' and a root-rot-from-overwatering warning, with no watering cadence or dry-down statement. Its tag '#drought tolerant' is a tolerance trait, not a watering instruction.
Soil pH, fertilizing, edibility and pollinator attraction are not addressed on the page. The Attributes block has no Attracts field and no mention of eating.

mature_height_in_max is 6, from 'up to 6 inches in height' (a single figure, so the minimum is left null). The same sentence says the plant 'will grow to 1 to 2 feet in length', which is trailing-stem length, not a spread, so the spread fields are null.
NC State lists 'Variegata' as a cultivar. No cultivar data was used.
NC State's Common Name(s) list is alphabetized (Cupid Peperomia, Vining Peperomia). Its first entry, Cupid Peperomia, is used as common_name; the description prose uses 'Vining Peperomia'.

records.name_note: Sources both lead with Mosaic Calathea: NC State's alphabetized Common Name(s) list gives Mosaic Calathea then Network Prayer Plant, while its description prose calls the plant the network prayer plant, and RHS's plant profile shows mosaic calathea as the common name. NC State lists Calathea bella, Calathea musaica, Maranta kegeljanii, Maranta musaica and Maranta tessellata under 'Previously known as'; RHS's Synonyms field includes Calathea bella and Calathea musaica, and its page says 'Previously included within the genus Calathea'. The plant is filed here under Goeppertia.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State (description prose, not a Poison block): "The network plant is non-toxic to pets and humans; however, the sap can cause skin irritation. Wear protective gloves when handling this plant." Its tag list, reproduced in full, is: #clumping #partial shade tolerant #non-toxic for cats #perennial #houseplant #evergreen #humidity tolerant #interesting leaves #contact dermatitis #erect #acidic soils tolerant #non-toxic for dogs #fast growing #container plant. The page names no poison part and no symptom list; the 'pets' wording in the prose is unscoped, while the cat and dog scope comes from the separate tags non-toxic for cats and non-toxic for dogs. Its Problems field reads Contact Dermatitis. RHS does not address toxicity.
unknowns: No MoBot, UF/IFAS, Clemson, Penn State, UMD or UGA page for this exact taxon was found; only NC State and RHS were used (RHS also has separate pages for the 'Network' cultivar listing and 'Pp0005'; only the species page was used).
day_f/night_f null: NC State gives one combined range of 60 to 80 F with no day/night split; RHS gives none.
chill_damage_f null: NC State says frost intolerant and hardy in USDA zones 11 to 12, which is a hardiness rating, not a damage-onset temperature.

light_fc and direct_sun_hours_max null: NC State's Light field is Partial Shade with a generic 2-6 hours legend parenthetical, not species prose. RHS's structured Position field gives only Partial shade; its "bright indirect or filtered light" line is shared genus Cultivation text.
soil_ph null: NC State lists Acid (<6.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0) and RHS says Acid or Alkaline or Neutral, so neither a floor nor a ceiling is supported.

water_regime null: NC State says 'Water regularly with distilled water or rain water', which gives no dry-down rule. RHS's 'Water moderately when in growth ... keep just moist in winter' is shared genus Cultivation text (identical on the RHS Goeppertia rufibarba page), not species guidance. Interval and dry-down fields left null.

fertilize fields null: NC State says 'Fertilize the plant every month during the growing season with a balanced houseplant fertilizer.', a word cadence with no dilution fraction or named months. RHS's 'apply a balanced liquid fertiliser monthly' is shared genus Cultivation text and was not used.
is_edible and attracts_pollinators null: no admissible source addresses eating or pollinators; NC State flowers are insignificant.

RHS's structured size bands are 0.5-1 metres (19.7-39.4 in) for height and spread, but its description says "to 60cm" (about 23.6 in), consistent with NC State's 1 to 2 feet; NC State's figures were used as the anchor.

Toxicity: NC State prose says non-toxic to 'pets and humans' (unscoped) while the sap may cause skin irritation (tag contact dermatitis); cat/dog scope rests on the two tags. No other admissible source addresses toxicity.

common_name: researched as 'Network Prayer Plant'; landed as 'Mosaic Calathea', the first entry of NC State's alphabetized Common Name(s) list and the common name RHS's plant profile shows. NC State's description prose uses 'network prayer plant', kept as the alternate in name_note.

normalizations: 2026-10-09: b126 (common houseplants) landed on branch claude/database-build-goals-e548af from the post-audit records. Eight species: Beautiful Hoya (Hoya bella), Furry Feather Calathea (Goeppertia rufibarba, formerly Calathea rufibarba), Devil's Backbone (Euphorbia tithymaloides, formerly Pedilanthus tithymaloides), False Aralia (Plerandra elegantissima, formerly Dizygotheca/Schefflera elegantissima), Flaming Sword (Lutheria splendens, formerly Vriesea splendens), Cupid Peperomia (Peperomia serpens), Button Fern (Hemionitis rotundifolia, formerly Pellaea rotundifolia), Mosaic Calathea (Goeppertia kegeljanii). Auditor-supplied corrected wording used verbatim (Furry Feather Calathea's name_note drops only its 'matching its page-title parenthetical' clause, a <title>-only fact); every substitute quote ground-truthed with qc.py and a strict consecutive-node / <body>-only check. Landing decisions: NC State's '(Name, Name)' page-title parenthetical exists only in <title> on every page here, so all such quotes were replaced with rendered Common Name(s) list items, the H1 binomial or description prose; toxic_to_pets rests on separate '#non-toxic for cats' / '#non-toxic for dogs' (or '#problem for ...') tags and full tag-run quotes are newline-stacked as the page renders them; RHS's bare Name Status 'Correct' kept in the CORR form paired with RHS's page title (the audit had asked to drop it on False Aralia and Mosaic Calathea); Devil's Backbone full_sun dropped on the species burn warning (part_shade only) and its full Poison block quoted; Button Fern soil_base set to ericaceous on the audit's acidic-mix reading; Mosaic Calathea's genus-level RHS Cultivation quotes dropped. No common_name collides with an already-landed record. MoBot was not used (it refuses non-browser clients from this machine).
